# windows_registry_key (Resource)

Manages a Windows registry key on a remote host over SSH + PowerShell: ensures the key exists, optionally purges unmanaged value names, and optionally removes the key on destroy.

The key resource never carries value payloads: manage each value with a `windows_registry_value` resource and list its name in `managed_value_names` so the purge does not delete it. Each hive/path/name has a single owner: list every name managed by windows_registry_value resources in managed_value_names. The key resource never sets value data; managing the same name from both resources is last-write-wins, so order the key after its values with depends_on when purge_unknown_values is true.

By default (`purge_unknown_values = false`, `delete_key_on_destroy = false`) the resource is a no-op towards unknown values and leaves the key in place on destroy.

Import example: `terraform import windows_registry_key.example 'HKLM\SOFTWARE\MyApp'`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    windows = {
      source  = "kfrlabs/windows"
      version = "~> 0.1"
    }
  }
}

provider "windows" {
  host     = var.windows_host
  username = var.windows_username
  password = var.windows_password
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Ensure a key exists, without touching values (defaults: no purge, the key
# is left in place on destroy)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
resource "windows_registry_key" "app" {
  hive = "HKLM"
  path = "SOFTWARE\\MyApp"

  # Bound every remote operation explicitly: without this block each
  # operation defaults to 10 minutes, and a stalled registry operation
  # surfaces a timeout diagnostic instead of blocking Terraform
  # indefinitely.
  timeouts = {
    create = "20m"
    read   = "5m"
    update = "20m"
    delete = "20m"
  }
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Opt-in purge: delete unmanaged value names, keep the managed ones
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
resource "windows_registry_value" "version" {
  hive         = "HKLM"
  path         = "SOFTWARE\\MyApp"
  name         = "Version"
  type         = "REG_SZ"
  value_string = "2.5.1"
}

resource "windows_registry_key" "managed" {
  hive = "HKLM"
  path = "SOFTWARE\\MyApp"

  # The purge set is the live enumeration MINUS managed_value_names. No
  # Terraform state outside this resource is consulted, so every name owned
  # by a windows_registry_value resource must be listed explicitly,
  # including "" for the Default value. Same hive/path/name must have a
  # single owner: managing one name from both resources is last-write-wins.
  purge_unknown_values = true
  managed_value_names  = ["Version"]

  depends_on = [windows_registry_value.version]
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Remove the whole key (including subkeys) on destroy
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
resource "windows_registry_key" "ephemeral" {
  hive = "HKCU"
  path = "SOFTWARE\\MyEphemeralApp"

  delete_key_on_destroy = true
  recursive             = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `hive` (String) Registry hive: HKLM, HKCU, HKCR, HKU, or HKCC (case-insensitive, normalised to uppercase). ForceNew. Warning: keys under a path containing a Policies segment (e.g. SOFTWARE\Policies or SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies) are typically enforced by Group Policy: purged values may be recreated and a deleted key may reappear after the next policy refresh.
- `path` (String) Subkey path under the hive (backslash-separated, no leading/trailing backslash). ForceNew. Warning: keys under a path containing a Policies segment (e.g. SOFTWARE\Policies or SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies) are typically enforced by Group Policy: purged values may be recreated and a deleted key may reappear after the next policy refresh.

### Optional

- `delete_key_on_destroy` (Boolean) When true, Destroy removes the key. Subkeys are only removed when recursive is also true. Default false: the key (and everything under it) is left in place on destroy.
- `managed_value_names` (List of String) Value names owned elsewhere (typically the name attributes of windows_registry_value resources targeting this key) and therefore excluded from the purge. Use "" for the Default (unnamed) value, consistently with windows_registry_value. Default: empty list.
- `purge_unknown_values` (Boolean) When true, Create and Update delete every live value name that is not listed in managed_value_names. The purge set is the live enumeration minus managed_value_names; no Terraform state outside this resource is consulted, so every managed name must be listed explicitly. Default false: unknown values are left in place and only reported in unknown_value_names. Each hive/path/name has a single owner: list every name managed by windows_registry_value resources in managed_value_names. The key resource never sets value data; managing the same name from both resources is last-write-wins, so order the key after its values with depends_on when purge_unknown_values is true.
- `recursive` (Boolean) Allow Destroy to remove the key tree including subkeys. Only takes effect with delete_key_on_destroy = true. Purging values never touches subkeys.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Composite ID: "<HIVE>\<PATH>".
- `unknown_value_names` (List of String) Preview of the purge: live value names not listed in managed_value_names. Populated on every Read; values are only deleted when purge_unknown_values is true.
- `value_names` (List of String) Live value names enumerated in the key. The Default (unnamed) value appears as "".

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Read operations occur during any refresh or planning operation when refresh is enabled.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import a registry key.
# Format: HIVE\PATH  (backslash-separated; quote to prevent shell interpretation)
terraform import windows_registry_key.app 'HKLM\SOFTWARE\MyApp'
```
